chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Safwan, from Mu'awiyah ibn 'Ammar, from al-Hakam ibn 'Utaybah, who said:

I said to Abi Ja'far عليه السلام: What do you say about a domesticated pigeon that was slaughtered outside the sanctuary and then brought into the Haram? He said: There is no problem in eating it if he was not in ihram; but if he was in ihram, then no. And he said: If it was brought into the Haram and then slaughtered there, then indeed it was slaughtered after it had entered its place of safety.

key_terms.الْحَرَمَ: the sacred sanctuary possessing inviolability and protection
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: the area outside the sacred sanctuary boundary
key_terms.ذُبِحَ: was slaughtered according to the act under discussion
key_terms.مَأْمَنَهُ: its place of safety and inviolable protection
key_terms.مُحِلًّا: a person not in the state of ihram
key_terms.مُحْرِمًا: a person in the state of ihram for hajj or 'umrah

ai.seo_question: Can a domesticated pigeon slaughtered outside the Haram be eaten inside it, and what if the person is in ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning the eating of a domesticated pigeon slaughtered outside or inside the Haram. It distinguishes between the state of being muhill and muhrim, and it also establishes that an animal brought into the Haram attains protection once it enters that sanctuary.
